engines.name: Electric, 77.4 kWh Long Range (RWD or AWD)

issues.t: Charging unit (ICCU) failure and loss of drive power (recall)
issues.sym: A 'Check electric vehicle system' or 12-volt battery warning appears, the car may refuse to charge, and it can lose drive power while moving. Some cars will not start at all because the 12-volt battery has gone flat.
issues.why: The Integrated Charging Control Unit (ICCU), which charges both the big drive battery and the small 12-volt battery, can be damaged by an electrical overload and blow its fuse. Once it stops topping up the 12-volt battery, the car's electronics shut down. Hyundai first recalled the cars in March 2024 and widened the recall in November 2024.
issues.next: Run your VIN through Hyundai's or NHTSA's recall lookup. If a warning appears, pull over safely and call Hyundai roadside assistance. The dealer inspects and replaces the ICCU and fuse as needed and updates the software for free, even if the car was fixed under the earlier recall.

issues.t: 12-volt battery goes flat and the car won't wake up
issues.sym: The car is completely dead, the doors may not unlock with the key fob, or it shows battery warnings, often after sitting a few days. Some owners replace the small battery well before it is two years old.
issues.why: The Ioniq 6 still uses a small 12-volt battery to wake up its computers. Hyundai issued a bulletin for weak 12-volt charging caused by an ICCU fault (code P1A9096), and some owners simply see the original battery wear out early.
issues.next: Jump-start or charge the 12-volt battery (the owner's manual shows where). If it keeps happening, ask the dealer to test the battery and check for the ICCU recall and bulletin 23-01-060H before paying for a new battery.

issues.sym: A clunk or bang from the rear followed by a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: The inner rear driveshaft on some cars may not have been heat-treated properly, so it can snap under load.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-065. The dealer replaces the rear inner driveshaft for free.

issues.t: Reduction gear bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the drive unit, loss of drive power, or in the worst case the wheels locking up.
issues.why: Bolts inside the differential (gear drive unit) on some cars may not have been tightened enough at the factory and can work loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-283. The dealer replaces the gear drive unit under the recall. Stop driving if you hear new grinding from the drive unit.

issues.t: Charging port door panel can fall off (recall)
issues.sym: The outer panel of the charging port door is loose or missing.
issues.why: The decorative outer panel on the charging port door may not be bonded well enough and can come off while driving, becoming a hazard for cars behind.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-606. The dealer adds adhesive to the charging port door for free.

issues.t: Front seat belt anchors may detach (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign. The lower seat belt anchor may feel loose, especially if the seat or belt was removed during earlier repairs.
issues.why: A snap-on part of the front seat belt's lower anchor can be damaged, often when it is taken off and put back during service, so the anchor may not stay attached in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-218. The dealer inspects the anchors and reinforces or replaces them for free. Owner letters went out from May 2026.

issues.t: 'Power is limited' warning with turtle light
issues.sym: A turtle-shaped warning light comes on with a 'Power is limited' message, and the car accelerates weakly.
issues.why: Hyundai issued bulletin 24-EV-003H for this condition, which can set trouble code P0A2F, a drive-motor temperature code.
issues.next: Have the dealer read the codes and check for bulletin 24-EV-003H. Drive gently until it is looked at, since power can drop further.

issues.t: Home Level 2 charging slows down or charge port gets hot
issues.sym: Home charging starts at the normal rate and then drops to about half speed, so a full charge takes roughly twice as long. Some owners measured very high temperatures at the charging inlet.
issues.why: Owners report the AC charging inlet overheating, and the car then cuts the charging current to protect itself.
issues.next: Check that the charger plug and the car's port are clean and undamaged. If charging keeps slowing down, have the dealer inspect the charging inlet and install any charging software updates. Stop using a port that is discolored or smells hot.

issues.t: Charging port insulation caps missing or damaged
issues.sym: Small caps inside the charging port are missing or broken, and charging may throw errors.
issues.why: Hyundai bulletin 23-EV-006H tells dealers to inspect the charging port and replace missing or damaged insulation caps, which protect the pins from water and dirt.
issues.next: Look inside the port. If caps are missing, ask the dealer to apply bulletin 23-EV-006H.

issues.t: Brake lights and i-Pedal behave oddly during regenerative braking
issues.sym: The brake lights may not come on as expected when the car slows hard on regenerative braking, or one-pedal (i-Pedal) driving feels inconsistent.
issues.why: Hyundai released a vehicle control unit software update (bulletin 23-01-067H-1) that changes the brake-light logic during regenerative braking and how i-Pedal mode works.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to confirm the vehicle control software update has been installed.

issues.t: Doors don't unlock as you walk up
issues.sym: The Smart Approach Unlock feature works only some of the time, so the doors stay locked as you walk up with the key.
issues.why: Hyundai bulletin 23-01-043H covers intermittent Smart Approach Unlock operation on some 2023 Ioniq 6 cars.
issues.next: Use the fob button or door handle sensor in the meantime and ask the dealer to apply bulletin 23-01-043H.

issues.t: Power trunk lid doesn't latch fully
issues.sym: The power trunk lid closes but doesn't latch properly, and a warning chime or open-trunk message stays on.
issues.why: Hyundai bulletin 23-01-059H covers a power tailgate (trunk) that does not latch correctly.
issues.next: Don't drive with the trunk unlatched. Ask the dealer to perform bulletin 23-01-059H.

issues.t: Wireless phone charger and digital key fail in hot weather
issues.sym: Phones won't charge on the wireless pad and the phone digital key may not work when the cabin is hot, such as after parking in the sun.
issues.why: Owners report the pad stops working until the interior cools down, likely heat protection in the charger.
issues.next: Cool the cabin first, keep the physical key card or fob with you, and report it to the dealer so any software updates can be applied.

issues.t: Car keeps showing 'plugged in' when unplugged
issues.sym: The display says the car is plugged in even after the cable has been removed.
issues.why: Owners report this display fault and dealers have not given a clear cause.
issues.next: Make sure the charging cable is fully removed and the port latch is released, then report it to the dealer with photos.
